purpose: Display understandable source lineage for material citizen-facing answer statements without exposing internal reasoning or restricted metadata.
core_principle: CLAIM → SOURCE → WHAT IT SUPPORTS → SCOPE → LIMITATION
rules: Every material citizen-facing claim should have an identifiable supporting source or approved evidential basis.
A source is displayed with the specific proposition, record or procedure it supports.
General official service pages are not presented as proof of property-specific facts.
Property-specific claims retain property and date match information where material.
Historical claims retain historical source/date/version context.
Case law is displayed with the proposition it actually supports, not a broader inferred rule.
Official guidance is distinguished from legislation.
Access limitations are disclosed where they affect verification.
Provenance display explains source lineage without exposing internal chain-of-thought.
hard_stops: Never imply a source supports more than it actually supports.
Never invent an exact provision, record reference, date or version.
Never use source prestige as a substitute for relevance or scope.
Never expose restricted documents or internal metadata.
Never present a provenance chain as proof when a required property-specific record is missing.
